name: Caskmarket Vendor's Full Concealment Street Set
description: A deep-pocketed vendor's apron in weathered rust-brown canvas over a nondescript gray thermal hoodie, loose-fit cargo trousers with sewn-in flex-panel hidden compartments rated for 4kg of concealed goods, and scuffed platform market boots with false-sole storage. The apron's front panels are lined with signal-scatter fabric that masks the thermal signature of contraband. This looks like someone selling street food — and sometimes they are.
functionality: Signal-scatter apron panels mask thermal contraband signatures; false-sole boot compartments and flex-panel trouser pockets hold up to 4kg of concealed product across distributed load points.
what_it_says: This person sells things — the question is whether any of it is legal.
manufacturer: Self-assembled (components from Rolen Surplus and Dockwall street stalls)
story_hooks: The thermal-masking apron is also hiding a medical condition the wearer can't afford to have scanned at a checkpoint.
A regular customer hands over the wrong payment chip — it contains encrypted data worth more than anything the dealer has ever moved.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately anonymous street vendor silhouette—slouched, bulky, deliberately unglamorous. The layered construction creates visual noise and breaks up body shape. At first glance: food cart operator. Closer inspection: tactical concealment architecture. Wide, heavy stance.
physical_description.fit: Intentionally oversized and shapeless—cargo trousers hang loose from hip, hoodie swallows frame, apron drapes without definition. Compression panels hidden under loose outer layers. Silhouette designed to distribute weight and conceal volume changes.
physical_description.primary_material: Rust-brown weathered canvas apron (14oz, stained with food and oxidation), gray synthetic-wool thermal hoodie (brushed fleece-backed), ballistic-weave cargo trousers (treated for stain resistance), scuffed synthetic leather market boots (reinforced toe and heel).
physical_description.texture: Canvas: rough, broken-in, faded unevenly with genuine wear. Hoodie: soft napped surface, pilled in high-friction areas. Cargo weave: slightly stiff, utilitarian. Boots: creased leather, salt-stained, sole deeply worn. Signal-scatter lining: faint metallic thread pattern visible under direct light.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant rust-brown canvas with deep charcoal-gray hoodie. Muted earth tones—no contrast, nothing flashy. Boots in scuffed tan-gray. Subtle bronze threading in signal-scatter panels barely visible.
physical_description.closures: Apron: friction-fit over shoulders, side-snap closures (industrial-grade, replaceable). Hoodie: half-zip with rubberized pulls. Cargo trousers: magnetic fly (silent, no metallic sound), snap-waist (adjustable for load distribution). Boot laces: flat gray cordage, utilitarian knots.
distinctive_features: Apron front lined with signal-scatter fabric (thermal signature masking)
8 deep cargo pockets in apron—4 exterior (vendor supplies), 4 interior (concealment rated)
Flex-panel hidden compartments in trouser legs (sewn-in, 4kg capacity per leg)
False-sole storage in boots (pressure-plate access, ~500g per boot)
Reinforced seams throughout—industrial-grade thread, visible stress stitching
Thermally-treated inner lining resists moisture and odor retention
Wear patterns authentic: fraying at cuffs, faded knee panels from kneeling, smudged apron from handling
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 sub-grade. Street-level, self-assembled, sourced from surplus. No new components. Zero corporate finishing. Every element is functional salvage.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street vendor, black market operator, underground economy. The uniform of someone who moves goods—legal or otherwise—through the Caskmarket district. Wears this to blend into the vendor class, to be invisible in plain sight. Signals: 'I work the streets, I move things, ask no questions.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Genuinely weathered and patched. Canvas shows authentic food stains and oxidation. Seams reinforced with field repairs. Boots scuffed from market floors. Hoodie pills and fades. No pristine elements—the condition IS the camouflage.
